description: Imports an OWL ontology file (RDF/XML or JSON-LD) and converts it to the Fabric Ontology definition format. Compatible with Ontology Playground catalogue .rdf files.
notes: Detects format from file extension (.rdf/.owl → RDF/XML, .jsonld/.json → JSON-LD) or content sniffing. Use --output-dir instead of --workspace/--id for local export only (no API call). Supports owl:Class → EntityType, owl:DatatypeProperty → properties, owl:ObjectProperty → RelationshipType, ont:isIdentifier → entityIdParts, ont:isTimeSeries → timeseriesProperties, ont:isUntyped → untypedProperties (valueType Any), rdfs:subClassOf → baseEntityTypeId (entity type inheritance). Type/property/relationship names are sanitized to the schema pattern ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,127}$ (e.g. 'has site' → 'has_site'). By default this generates only the type schema; add --lakehouse (and optionally --bindings) to also generate DataBindings and relationship Contextualizations so the ontology is queryable. `ontology export` round-trips these annotations back to OWL.

binding_example.description: Import an ontology AND bind every entity/relationship type to data-source tables in one call. Generated DataBindings and Contextualizations conform to the official Fabric schemas (item/ontology/dataBinding and contextualization). Entity DataBindings default by convention (table = lowercased class name, source column = property label); the binding map overrides those and supplies relationship key columns. Binding IDs are deterministic (UUIDv5) so re-imports update in place.
binding_example.default_source_flags: The default data source can be set entirely by flags: --lakehouse $ID (+ --lakehouse-workspace, --lakehouse-schema) for a LakehouseTable source, or --eventhouse $ID --cluster-uri $URI --database $DB --timestamp-column $COL (+ --eventhouse-workspace) for a KustoTable/Eventhouse TimeSeries source. --lakehouse and --eventhouse are mutually exclusive; mix sources per-entity via the --bindings source blocks.
binding_example.notes: sourceColumns/targetColumns are arrays: one column per entityIdParts entry, so composite keys are supported. dataBindingType is 'NonTimeSeries' (default, LakehouseTable only) or 'TimeSeries' (LakehouseTable or KustoTable/Eventhouse, requires timestampColumn). Properties listed in entities.<name>.timeseriesProperties are emitted under the entity's timeseriesProperties; the rest stay static properties. An entity may have MULTIPLE data bindings via entities.<name>.bindings[] (e.g. a static NonTimeSeries Lakehouse table plus a telemetry TimeSeries Eventhouse table) — each binding picks its properties via columns/properties, or defaults by type (NonTimeSeries→static, TimeSeries→time-series+identifier). entities.<name>.baseEntityType names the parent entity type (overrides rdfs:subClassOf). entities.<name>.documents [{displayText?, url}] and entities.<name>.resourceLinks [{type?, workspaceId, itemId}] add entity Documents/ResourceLinks parts. Relationship Contextualizations must use a LakehouseTable source. Generated DataBindings force sourceType as the first key in sourceTableProperties, as the Fabric API requires. Relationships absent from the map emit a type with no contextualization (a warning is printed).
